name: Min Bei Chinese
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Norman, Jerry. 1969. The Kienyang dialect of Fukien. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley (phonological description of a Min Bei variety); not found online.

new_statements.citation: one of the works listed for this language (see the second reader's note)
new_statements.check: reported by the second reader, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed for this item and it was opened and read, so a two-work spot-check of unopened or silent works is not possible; I re-searched that work's full text and text layer for all stress terms and found nothing beyond what the reader reports. As a check on the reader's conflicts note I also a full-text search for stress/accent the three sources saved earlier in the same directory: Shen 2016 (Jianyang) mentions stress only inside quotations of Roengpitya 2007 (p. 44) and Pierrehumbert 2000b (p. 97), neither about Jianyang; Shen 2012 (Shibei) has 'Shibei accent' (informant description) and a bibliography entry only; Wang 2020 (Jian'ou, Chinese text layer present, 22 hits for 声调…

sources.citation: Shen, Ruiqing. 2016. Tonal variation: a quantitative study of Jianyang Min Chinese. PhD thesis, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. DOI 10.14711/thesis-b1585053 (hdl 1783.1/97144).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 2 describes Jianyang Min phonology: 8 citation tones, TBU = syllable (printed pp. 24-25); instrumental study of tone in isolated vs connected forms. Nothing on word stress/accent; the word 'stress' appears only in quotations of Roengpitya 2007 (p. 44) and Pierrehumbert 2000 (p. 97).

sources.citation: Wikipedia articles 'Jian'ou dialect', 'Northern Min', 'Shaowu dialect' (raw wikitext, 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Tone tables only (Jian'ou 6 tones, Shaowu 6 tones); no stress statement; bibliographies point to Norman 1988 'Chinese', Yuan Jiahua 汉语方言概要, Lien 1990, Fujian gazetteer 方言志 (dead link; Internet Archive copy is only the site shell).

sources.citation: 王泊钧 Wang Bojun. 2020. 福建建瓯方言单、双音节声学分析 [Acoustic analysis of monosyllables and disyllables in the Jian'ou dialect]. ChinaXiv preprint 202011.00034v1 (Peking University).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Jian'ou has six citation tones (43, 31, 33, 44, 35, 42); the 36 disyllabic tone combinations 'basically keep the citation tones' (双字调基本上与原调保持一致, PDF p. 20). No mention of 轻声 (neutral tone) or 重音 (stress).

sources.citation: Shen, Ruiqing. 2012. Exploring phonetic properties of Northern Min: a case study of Shibei. MPhil thesis, HKUST. DOI 10.14711/thesis-b1197926 (hdl 1783.1/7659).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Shibei (Pucheng county) Northern Min: nine non-stopped tones contrasting in pitch, duration and phonation; 'voiced' initials realised differently word-initially vs word-medially. No statement on stress (Steed 2006 on stress in Longquan Wu is cited only for phonation).

sources.citation: Walton, A. Ronald. 1986. The Taishun phonological system: a descriptive study of a Northeastern Min dialect. In McCoy & Light (eds), Contributions to Sino-Tibetan Studies, Leiden: Brill, pp. 428-435 (Rosetta Project excerpt filed under mnp).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mis-filed by the Rosetta Project as 'Chinese, Min Bei': Taishun is a Min Dong (Northeastern Min) dialect of Zhejiang, not Min Bei. Tone system and glottic tension in Tone IIIA; nothing on stress. Kept only as a record of the mis-attribution.

sources.citation: Norman, Jerry L. 1971. A guide to the Chien-yang dialect. Princeton: Princeton University, Chinese Linguistics Project. 396 pp. (with Norman 1969, The Kienyang dialect of Fukien, PhD Berkeley, OCLC 3080007).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The most detailed English description of a core Min Bei variety (Jianyang); named by the earlier scan; a 396-page guide would state whether stress/neutral tone plays any role.

sources.citation: Pan, Weishui 潘渭水. 2007. 閩北方言研究 [Studies on Min Bei dialects]. 福州: 福建教育出版社. 263 pp.

sources.note: Glottolog's grammar sketch for Min Bei by the native-speaker co-author of the Jian'ou dictionary; Chinese-language descriptions of this type usually include a section on 輕聲 (neutral tone).

sources.citation: Ngai, Sing Sing. 2021. A Grammar of Shaowu: A Sinitic Language of Northwestern Fujian. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Chapter 3 'Phonology', pp. 31-46.

sources.note: The only modern full grammar under this glottocode; its phonology chapter is where a statement on stress/neutral tone in Shaowu would be (Shaowu is a Min-Gan hybrid, so its testimony may not transfer to Jian'ou/Jianyang).
